notes: Built from the 3000 BCE map, adjusted to 2500.

The age of the pyramids: Egypt was in the Old Kingdom, after the Great Pyramid of Khufu (about 2560). Sumer was a land of rival city-states, two centuries before Sargon of Akkad; Ebla and Mari were great cities in Syria.
The Indus Valley civilisation was in its mature phase (about 2600–1900), the age of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.

In Europe the Corded Ware culture had replaced the Baden and Cucuteni–Trypillia cultures, and on the steppe the Catacomb culture followed the Yamnaya. In China the Longshan cultures followed Yangshao and Dawenkou.
Dates this early are uncertain, often by a century.
Mesopotamia c. 3000 BCE was a patchwork of Sumerian city-states (Uruk, Ur, Kish), not a kingdom of Ur.
The Hurrian kingdoms date from after 2300 BCE.
The mature Indus cities date from c. 2600 BCE.
The Bantu expansion began c. 1500 BCE; in 3000 BCE Bantu speakers lived around the Nigeria–Cameroon border.
Filled the rest of the world with the hunter-gatherer and farming peoples of the 2000 BCE map.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Peoples of the deep past are named for their time: early modern humans, the Iberomaurusian and Capsian cultures, foragers before farming and herding spread.
The Caribbean islands were settled from about 5000 BCE (the Bahamas from about 700 CE): Archaic peoples, then the Saladoid peoples and the Taíno.
Mesoamerica is named for its peoples and states of the time.
